name: Reconstructed butcher shop (butcher)

documented_range.note: NO EVIDENCE ESTABLISHES THAT THIS PARTICULAR BUILDING EXISTED. It is the roof a reconstructed household requires - a meat market on the built streets, because a town of 3,265 does not walk three kilometres up the North Branch to Clybourne's for its dinner. The argument for the trade's presence in the town is in the household record and in the occupation census at data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json; the argument for THIS BUILDING is only that the household needs somewhere to be.

position.symbolic_location: South Division, local ENU E 659 N -132
position.note: INTERPRETIVE PLACEMENT, NOT A RECOVERED LOT. A meat market on the built streets, because a town of 3,265 does not walk three kilometres up the North Branch to Clybourne's for its dinner. The band follows ROADMAP K1's placement rule - businesses toward the river and the built streets, residences further out - using the same frontage bands the reconstruction recipes already work in, which come from the 80 ft platted street module in data/traces/street_control.json. The centre was tested against every structure footprint in the dataset, against the reserved slots of the two uninstantiated phase-2 recipes, against the platted street corridors of the K7 block grid so that no invented building stands in the roadway, and against the committed heightfield for coverage, dry ground and step tolerance; it is free ground and nothing more. The dataset's 20 m working georeference uncertainty applies on top of an already invented position.

derivation.reason: No source gives this building a lot. The placement is a frontage-band assignment tested for clearance and buildable ground, which is a production control and not a derivation from any line in the dataset.

footprint.note: A 18 x 26 ft rectangle from the C1 family band in the reconstruction specification. NO DIMENSION IS DOCUMENTED for this building, which does not exist in any source; the band is type-level evidence about what buildings of this class measured and is not evidence about this one.

THE OTHER FORM ON OFFER IS REFUSED, AND HERE IS THE NUMBER. The C1 roof line offers "front gable or shed, 5:12-9:12", and this town builds only the gable. A shed is one plane over the whole 8.4 m of this plan where a gable climbs half of it, so across the 441 plans C1's own footprint band allows, 231 of them cannot reach the 15-20 ft ridge band the same family authors — at any eave in its 9-11 ft band and at any pitch between 22.6 and 36.9 degrees. This building's own plan is one of them.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED BUILDING, RAISED FOR A RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). A meat market on the built streets, because a town of 3,265 does not walk three kilometres up the North Branch to Clybourne's for its dinner. It is NOT one of the anonymous count-units of the 665-roof programme: those are placed by aggregate mix and carry no occupant, while this one exists because the occupation census says the town held a household of this trade and no anonymous roof of the right family stood free in this district. It consumes one slot of its district's programme target rather than adding to it - see the accounting block in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json.
